mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which supports equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 20-day period following any date when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, the S&P 500 fails to produce positive returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (more than 0.2 percentage points over the past 3 months) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE increases by more than 0.2pp over 3 months, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 0.5% MoM) and insufficient monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) signals market anticipation of aggressive policy response, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 0.5% MoM and FEDFUNDS < 1.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market recovery (HOUST > 1800 thousand units), increased housing activity signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when HOUST > 1800 thousand units, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in industrial production (INDPRO > 100) reflects robust manufacturing activity and economic growth, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO > 100, the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS falls > 100k in 3 months) signals economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS falls by more than 100k over 3 months, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real personal consumption (RSAFS < 650000 million dollars) signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS < 650000, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%) with aggressive monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 2.5%), the market anticipates reduced corporate profits and higher discount rates, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.
